title: Modules
body: A module is a reusable BoxLang package. It can provide functions, classes, components and settings, with an optional native backend for MatchBox. Using a module Install a MatchBox-compatible package in boxlang_modules/ , or select its directory explicitly: matchbox --module ./libs/greeter app.bxs Project modules take precedence over shared packages in BOXLANG_HOME/modules/ . title: Native Builds
body: Build a standalone executable with the MatchBox runner and your compiled BoxLang code. The destination does not need a separate MatchBox installation or Java for ordinary BoxLang execution. title: Native Fusion example
body: Native Fusion lets you write performance-critical functions and stateful objects in Rust and use them directly from BoxLang. Everything is statically linked into a single native binary - no external libraries, no FFI boilerplate at call sites. title: Native Fusion reference
body: Native Fusion links Rust functions and objects into your BoxLang application. It supports every MatchBox target: native, browser/JavaScript, WASI and ESP32. Rust code and dependencies must support the selected target. Browser builds cannot use desktop OS APIs, and ESP32 code must fit the device. WASI remains experimental . title: Running work at the same time
body: A future stands for a value that is not ready yet. runAsync starts some work and hands you a future straight away. You call get() on it when you need the result. title: Sets
body: A set holds each value once. Create one with a literal, setNew() , setOf() or toSet() . title: Values and strings
body: Variables You create a variable by assigning to it. title: Welcome to MatchBox
body: BoxLang is a dynamic language for building applications. It normally runs on the JVM. MatchBox is a second runtime for the same language, written in Rust. It compiles your code to bytecode and runs it on a small virtual machine, which lets BoxLang go places the JVM does not fit: a single native executable, a browser tab, a serverless function, even a microcontroller.
